messages.subject: Rankselect items are not scored
parts:
Dear Community,

I'm currently trying to implement items of type 'rankselect'. So, I have multiple options and answers for each question. However, even though the raw_responses string (in the 'results' object) matches the answer in my .csv file, the score is always 0.

As you can see in the .csv attached, the Answer column has a string with the right answers for each question: 2;4;5;1;3. I've also tried providing one answer per column (Answer.1: 2; Answer.2: 4, etc.) but I get the following error: Warning: Error in if: the condition has length > 1

Thanks for your time and consideration.

Micaela

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Rankselect items are not scored
parts:
This is in part by design, though I have not documented why I chose this as the default behaviour. I've now added the following to the @param df documentation under the Answers element:

#'     \item{\code{Answer} or \code{Answer.#}}{(Optional) A character vector (or multiple character
#'       vectors) indicating the scoring key for items that have correct answer(s). If there
#'       is no correct answer for a question then a value of \code{NA} must be declared.
#'
#'       Note that 'scoring' some item response data can be ambiguous depending on the stimuli provided, which
#'       requires greater attention. For example, when using \code{'rankselect'}: should partial scoring
#'       be used if the ranks are mostly correct; should partial scoring be used if the response are
#'       only off by a ranking constant (e.g., correct rank is 1-2-3-4-5, but the respondent ranks 2-3-4-5-1, in which
#'       case four relative rankings are correct but 1 is incorrect); should a 0-1 scoring be used to indicate none-all correct?.
#'       When this type of ambiguity exists in the multiple-answers cases it is strongly recommended
#'       to use the \code{AnswerFuns} argument instead for better functional control

Hence, rankselect has a great deal of ambiguity in the proper way to score such response vectors, so it is best to define your own way of scoring such inputs manually instead. HTH for now.

Phil
